text:
Loop Fence Puzzle · Four-Player Free-for-All

Everyone solves the same 7×7 puzzle, drawing lines and X marks on their own image.
Connect only horizontally or vertically adjacent dots. Each number from 0 to 3 specifies how many of that cell’s four sides must have lines.
Blank cells do not restrict the number of lines. Every dot used must connect to exactly 2 lines.
Create a single closed loop with no branches, crossings, or dead ends. You do not need to pass through every dot.
An X is a private note marking a side where you will not draw a line; it is not part of the loop.

Only you can see your answer. When you think it is complete, press the buzzer to have your current answer checked.
The first 3 players to submit correct loops secure survival in that order. The remaining player is eliminated.
Everyone works on the same puzzle until the game ends. There are no separate rounds or overall time limit.
If your answer fails the check, you may erase or revise it and submit again. This is the retry policy for this simulation.
Buzzer presses in the same thinking interval are processed in order of shortest recorded response time. Ties follow the
seed-based priority order announced at the start. Once the third survivor is determined, later buzzer presses are not processed.
The survivors’ answers and the correct loop are revealed to everyone only after the game ends with 3 survivors.

Each time, submit a JSON action that replaces your entire answer.
{"type":"draw","edges":[["H",0,0]],"crosses":[["V",0,0]],"submit":false}
In the example above, H connects (row 0, column 0) to (row 0, column 1), and V connects (row 0, column 0) to (row 1, column 0).
Rows and columns use the image’s dot coordinates from 0 to 7; H columns and V rows range from 0 to 6.
edges lists the sides where you draw lines, and crosses lists the sides where you place X marks. A side cannot have both a line and an X.
When revising, include every line and X you want to keep. Omitted marks are erased. crosses may be omitted.
With submit:true, the buzzer is pressed to submit the answer immediately after it is drawn; with false, only your work is saved.
{"type":"wait"} leaves your current answer unchanged. A format error also preserves your current answer; it is not corrected into a valid solution.
There is no conversation, negotiation, or relationship evaluation. Once the model-call limit is reached, play continues with scripted demonstration actions.
